Panchakrosam — divine marriage of Shiva and Parvati (Aani)

history.dynasty: Lakolisa cult origin; rebuilt by Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara kings
history.period: 6th century CE onwards; hymned by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar (Paadal Petra Sthalam)
history.summary: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Lakolisa cult (twin of the Kayarohana temple in Gujarat), one of the Saptha Vidangam — Thyagaraja is worshipped here as Sundara Vidanga with the Paraavaara Tharanga Natanam, and his idol is of lapis lazuli. Legend says Shiva granted sage Pundari moksha with his body; to this day the sage's descendants' bodies are brought to the temple gate to be adorned with the lord's clothes and garlands. One of the Shakti Peethams (Neelayadakshi, 'the blue-eyed one'). (VERIFY: one source claims the original lingam was stolen and replaced by a gomedakam (hessonite) lingam; coordinates per Wikipedia, ~0.7 km from the geocoded temple arch.)

name: Kayarohanaswamy Temple
town_description: Nagapattinam is a coastal port town and district headquarters on the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu, with a fishing harbour and a Chola-era maritime past. It is a multi-faith pilgrimage hub — the Kayarohanaswamy and Soundararajaperumal temples, the Nagore Dargah and the nearby Velankanni church — about 25-80 km from Thanjavur and linked by rail and the East Coast Road.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport is the nearest major airport (verify distance)
travel.railway: Nagapattinam Junction, about 0.5 km north of the temple
travel.road: On the East Coast Road (ECR); buses to Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Karaikal and Chennai

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Adipooram (Aadi) is the signature festival
